Build your profile on a calmer day, with your device volume low. Every sound fades in, and hold-to-play sounds stop as soon as you let go. Still is for comfort and self-knowledge. It does not diagnose, treat or prevent migraine. Seek care for a new, sudden or different headache.

HOW ARE YOU RIGHT NOW?

Normal day: sounds play at your saved level.

Start with the questions, or jump to any step. Nothing plays until you press a button.

QUIET MODE

Only what you asked for.

Your comfort sound plays about 14 dB quieter than usual, with a softer top end, almost no swell and a slow fade-in of 6 seconds or more. Silence is always fine.

01 A FEW QUESTIONS · 30 SECONDS

What tends to bother you?

Your answers choose a gentle first sound. This is not a test or a diagnosis, and there are no right answers.

02 A QUIET REFERENCE · 30 SECONDS

Set your starting volume

Before you press play, turn your device volume down to about a quarter. Then play a soft, steady hush and adjust your device volume until it is quiet but clear: easy to hear, and nowhere near loud. Still measures every later sound relative to this point, because a browser cannot know the actual loudness at your ears.

Not set yet.

03 HEADPHONE CHECK · OPTIONAL · 1 MINUTE

Can you hear the hidden tone?

You will hear three short hisses. Over headphones, one of them contains a faint tone. Over speakers it mostly disappears. Six rounds; five correct confirms headphones. Stereo experiments in the sound lab rely on this.

Round 1 of 6

04 YOUR COMFORT CONTOUR · 2 MINUTES

Where is your ear most sensitive?

0 OF 7 BANDS

For each band, press and hold. The sound starts very quietly and rises slowly. Let go as soon as it stops feeling gentle. The sound stops the moment you let go, and it never goes above a fixed safe cap. Still then turns down the bands you mark lower, in every sound it makes for you.

05 FIND YOUR COMFORT SOUND · 3–5 MINUTES

Which one feels calmer?

ROUND 0

Each round plays two six-second sounds, A then B, at the same loudness. Pick the one that feels calmer. Still learns your preferences from these choices and moves the next pair toward what works for you. About 10–16 rounds is usually enough. Stop whenever you like.

HOW THIS WORKS, AND ITS LIMITS

Comparisons, not scores

“Which is calmer?” is easier to answer consistently than “rate this 1–10”. A Gaussian-process preference model (Chu & Ghahramani, 2005) learns from your choices and picks each new pair where it expects to learn the most. A similar approach has tuned hearing aids from 10–20 comparisons.

Four things that differ between people

How dark or bright the sound is (spectral tilt), noise versus a soft hum, how steady it is, and how soft the top end is. Annoyance research ranks loudness and sharpness first, and slow, regular changes are gentler than fast flutter.

States, not one setting

In lab studies, people with migraine found sound aversive at lower levels than controls, and at lower levels still during attacks. Still keeps one profile and adjusts it for your current state. The offsets are cautious starting points, not measurements of you.

What it cannot tell you

Preferring a sound is not the same as it reducing pain. Before-and-after pain changes also reflect time, medication and expectation. Your profile describes comfort, on your device, today. Evidence and sources ↗
